answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate is severe and the 14-day window is tight. Memory_c6 showed that multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing without narrowing scope—critical under cost pressure. Memory_c4 demonstrated that renegotiation at renewal recovered real margin and moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms. Pulling these two records will confirm whether aggressive negotiation (rather than switching to the low-cost vendor from memory_c2, who has SLA reliability issues) can bridge the gap. The assembly line is at 94% capacity with no buffer, making delivery risk acute—memory_c2's three-of-four-quarters SLA misses disqualify sole-source switching. Negotiating_terms preserves the incumbent's integration stability (memory_c1) while pursuing the cost recovery that proved possible before (memory_c4). A standard_experiment scale allows structured negotiation with defined fallback positions. Downstream risk is flagged because if negotiation fails within the 14-day window, there is limited time to execute an alternative. Uncertainty is preserved by keeping switching and second-sourcing as post-decision options if terms cannot be met.
